title: Daily Walkaround Check: Outside the Cab
whatItIs: Before your journey, walk round the lorry and trailer: lights, leaks, tyres, brake lines, coupling, load, plates and markings. Report any defects in writing.
keyFacts: You're responsible for making sure your vehicle is safe to drive. Do the walkaround check before your journey.

keyFacts.text: A driver or responsible person MUST do a walkaround check before the vehicle is used: at least once in every 24 hours.

keyFacts: Check the tyres have at least 1 mm of tread, no deep sidewall cuts and no cord visible anywhere.
Stop lamps should come on when you press the service brake and go out when you release it.
After the first brake test, leave the engine running: air pressure builds and leaks are easier to hear.
If you change trailers during the day, check each trailer you use.

visual.caption: Outside the vehicle: what to look for

items.title: Lights and indicators
items.text: All work. Lenses fitted, clean and the right colour. Marker lights work.

items.title: Fuel and oil leaks
items.text: Filler cap fitted correctly. Engine on: look underneath for leaks.

items.title: Tyres and wheel fixing
items.text: Tread at least 1 mm, correct pressure, wheel nuts tight, nothing between twins.

items.title: Brake lines and coupling
items.text: No air leaks or worn lines. Trailer secure in the fifth wheel, locks in place.

items.title: Body, guards and load
items.text: Doors, panels and guards secure. The load isn't moving or likely to move.

items.title: Plates, reflectors, markings
items.text: Number plate clean and complete. Reflectors and markings visible, right colour.

a.label: Daily walkaround check
points: Driver or responsible person, before use
At least once in every 24 hours in service

b.label: Safety inspection
points: Intervals as declared for the operator licence
Covers at least the annual test items

onTheTest.question: You've finished the first brake test of your walkaround check. What should you do with the engine for the rest of the check?
options: Switch it off to save fuel
Leave it running so pressure builds and air leaks are easier to hear
Rev it hard to test the exhaust smoke
Switch it off so you can hear the radio
onTheTest.why: DVSA advises leaving the engine running after the initial brake test so pressure can build up. This makes it easier to hear any leaks during the rest of the check.

onTheTest.question: You couple up to a different trailer halfway through your shift. What should you do?
options: Nothing: the morning check covers the whole day
Only check the trailer's number plate
Do a walkaround check of the new trailer before using it
onTheTest.why: Where trailers are changed during the day, a check should be made on each trailer being used.

traps: Fuel and oil leaks are checked with the engine on: look underneath the vehicle, not just at the filler cap.
Stop lamps should come on with the brake AND go out when you release it.
Look between twin wheels too: no objects or debris should be trapped there.
Not happy with the load? Ask the person in charge of vehicle safety to have it assessed and resecured.
